evidence: ArtifactData list of collection "state" on both artifacts, read 2026-09-23: ISA Portal (9Jtqg2W1t98PfhNYHNTMDS) 14 documents, Command Deck (3jbdGMNFkGLEpJiZ3cTmZW) 174 documents. Byte-comparison of the decoded v values: pipeline identical=True (2 entries both sides), reClients identical=True (2 entries), isaLine identical=True (10 entries), isaDailySchedule identical=True, isaKpi identical=False. ratesSnapshot syncedAt: portal 2026-09-22T02:24:25Z, deck 2026-09-22T20:30:08Z. The document is an empty list and has not changed since 2026-09-12 ... NOT synced — Steven's deck shows no mortgage pipeline at all" — the page's own two columns contradicting each other in the same row.

The false-green paragraph now rests on what the routine has NOT written rather than on two documents that have since appeared, and the bridge row cites routineHealth's recorded lastRun plus the later convergence, saying plainly that neither page records the exact time. SYSTEMIC FIX, so this cannot rot silently again: a new driftFooterHtml() prints the far-side column's age on every render and, past DRIFT_STALE_AFTER_DAYS (3), replaces the footer with a red block reading "The Command Deck column is N days old — treat it as unverified". Both paths executed: at today's stamp it reads "Measured today."; with the stamp forced to 2026-09-13 it reads the red 9-day warning.

area: isa-portal.html and command-deck.html — showings: shState(), shSyncReqs() and their call sites
finding: The crash guard the brief asked me to look for, in its exact shape, on BOTH pages — and worse than the health-coaching one, because these renders are called from a plain IIFE rather than from safeRun, so the throw was a TOP-LEVEL exception that killed every render after it instead of costing one card. Three separate document shapes trigger it: showingSyncRequests[].targets written as a string ("(r.targets || []).join is not a function"), showingSyncRequests[].payload missing ("Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'addr')"), and showingSchedule.clients[].showings written as a string ("(c.showings || []).filter is not a function"). `x || []` defends against null and undefined only; a TRUTHY non-array sails straight through it and then throws on the array method. shState() guarded s.clients with Array.isArray but nothing one level down, and shSyncReqs() returned the raw document with no guard at all.
evidence: runtime-harness --inject, 2026-09-23. ISA Portal, baseline 47 containers: targets-as-string → top-level exception at line 4523, 45 containers; payload-missing → top-level exception at line 4523, 45 containers; showings-as-string → top-level exception at line 4492, 42 containers. Command Deck, baseline 338 containers: the same three inputs → top-level exceptions at lines 26994 and 26963, dropping to 321, 321 and 318 containers — twenty panels dark from one malformed field. All six were exceptions, not safeRunFailures: nothing caught them.
fix: Guarded the SHAPE once at the source on both pages rather than at the dozen call sites that reach into it — the rule the deck's own lsShapeWarn comment already states, applied one level further down. Added shArr(); shState() now rejects a non-object document, drops non-object clients and coerces every client's showings to an array; shSyncReqs() rejects a non-array document, drops non-object entries and coerces targets and payload on each one. Both record an lsShapeWarn so the mismatch is reportable rather than silent. Re-injected all three shapes plus two more (the document itself an object, the clients array holding junk): 0 exceptions, 0 safeRun failures, and containers hold at 47 and 338 in every case.

area: isa-portal.html — renderLoftyImport(), the Live CRM Import card
finding: A loftyLeads document of unrecognised shape made the card announce a completed sync that had never happened. With the document set to {a:1} the card rendered "Synced (no stamp on the document) · source: Lofty · 0 contacts across 0 stages · 0 created in the last 90 days." — which reads as a sync that ran and found nothing, when in truth nothing had been read at all. The status branch only caught the two strings it knew ("not-configured", "error"); anything else, including a non-string status, fell through to the success path. Command Deck's card, fed the identical document, correctly said "Awaiting the first Lofty sync" — so the two pages disagreed about the same document, and the portal was the wrong one.
evidence: runtime-harness --dump-text with --inject loftyLeads={"a":1}, 2026-09-23. ISA before: loftySyncNote = "Synced (no stamp on the document) · source: Lofty · 0 contacts across 0 stages · 0 created in the last 90 days." Command Deck, same input: "Awaiting the first Lofty sync — the Mac's lofty-bridge MCP is installed (status RUN)...". The deck's guard is the line `if (!totals.length && !loftyArr(d.newLeads90d).length) { loftyEmptyState(...); return; }`, which the portal had no equivalent of.
fix: Ported the deck's two guards to the portal: a non-string status is now reported as "unreadable" rather than ignored, any status other than ok short-circuits to an explaining empty state, and a document carrying neither stage totals nor a lead list is refused with "No Lofty counts in this document ... this card will not report a sync it cannot see". Five inputs executed after the fix — no document, garbage object, status not-configured, non-string status, and a well-formed live document — and each renders the honest line for its case, the real one still reading "Synced 2026-09-23T01:00:00Z · refreshed today · source: Lofty · 6 contacts across 2 stages · 1 created in the last 90 days."

area: isa-portal.html — lsGetSeeded(), the document reader behind every seeded panel
finding: The portal's lsGetSeeded had no shape guard and no corrupt-JSON signal: it returned whatever parsed, so a document written as a string where a list was expected was handed straight to the caller, and unparseable JSON fell back to the seed in complete silence. Command Deck's lsGetSeeded has guarded both for some time. This is why a corrupted isaVanessaChat cost a panel on the portal and nothing on the deck — the same class of drift as F-Q3-04, in the plumbing rather than in a card.
evidence: Fuzzing every document key the portal reads with four wrong shapes each (string, number, object-for-array, array-for-object), 2026-09-23: isaVanessaChat as a string → 1 safeRun failure, 46 of 47 containers. The portal already had LS_SHAPE_WARNINGS and a renderIsaStateWarnings() banner built — lsGetSeeded simply never called into them.
fix: Ported the deck's guard verbatim in shape: unparseable JSON now raises lsShapeWarn(key, "valid JSON", ...) before falling back, and a stored value whose type does not match the seed's falls back to the seed with the mismatch recorded. Also corrected the banner's wording, which said the bad value "was kept, not dropped" — with the guard in place it IS dropped for that render, so it now says the saved document is untouched but the page fell back to its built-in starting value and what you see may not be what you entered. After the fix the full fuzz across 20 document keys and four shapes each reports no exceptions, no safeRun failures and 47 of 47 containers in every single case.

area: isa-portal.html — isaStampAgeDays(), every panel-freshness badge on the page
finding: A stamp that outran its data, in the helper rather than in one panel. isaStampAgeDays anchored the stamp at LOCAL noon and subtracted milliseconds, which is wrong at both ends of the day: a panel checked YESTERDAY still read "today" for any viewer whose clock was before noon, and a stamp written TODAY measured -1, which only failed to show because isaStampRelative collapses anything <= 0 to "today". Any numeric consumer of the age gets the negative. Command Deck fixed this exact bug some time ago in execDaysOld, whose comment describes the same symptom ("printed -1d every morning until noon"); the portal was never brought along.
evidence: Observed while checking my own work: with the sync panel restamped 2026-09-23 the new drift footer printed "Measured -1 days ago." Under TZ=UTC the badge on panel-isa-loanprograms, stamped 2026-09-22, read "Part-checked today". Command Deck's execDaysOld already compares calendar days against the Pacific date with Math.round and clamps negatives to 0.
fix: Ported the deck's approach: added isaPtYmd() (Pacific date, from the deck's execPtYmd) and rewrote isaStampAgeDays to difference calendar days against the Pacific date, Math.round for DST, clamped at 0. Verified across a date range under TZ=UTC: 2026-09-23 and 2026-09-22 → "today" (the Pacific date is still the 22nd), 2026-09-21 → "yesterday", 2026-09-20 → "2d ago", 2026-09-13 → "1w ago", 2026-08-22 → "1mo ago". The drift footer now reads "Measured today." and reuses isaStampRelative rather than wording its own.

area: isa-portal.html — ISA_PANEL_VERIFIED_AT["panel-isa-syncstatus"], the one scope:"full" stamp in either artifact

fix: Restamped to scope "part", at 2026-09-23, with a note that names both halves as the schema requires: re-sourced today — both artifact databases' state collections read directly and every drift row corrected against them, four having gone wrong in a single day; NOT re-sourced — the Mac-side facts, which carry their own dates in the text. The note also records that the panel was "full" until today and why that over-claimed. Badge now reads "Part-checked today".

finding: Two more documents reaching an array method unguarded, both caught by safeRun rather than top-level, so each cost its own card silently. renderMarketSnapshot: lsGetSeeded guards the TOP-LEVEL shape only, so a marketSnapshot document that is an object passes even when the arrays the renderer needs are absent — data.indices.map then threw ("Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')"), and data.sources was read unguarded too. renderHealthMetrics: uses lsGet, the raw reader with no shape check at all, and called rows.sort directly — a healthMetrics document written as a string or object threw ("rows.sort is not a function").
evidence: Fuzzing 62 deck document keys with four wrong shapes each, 2026-09-23: marketSnapshot as an object → safeRun failure renderMarketSnapshot at line 22503, 336 of 338 containers; healthMetrics as a string, number or object → safeRun failure renderHealthMetrics, 337 of 338 containers.
fix: renderMarketSnapshot now normalises field by field against MARKET_SNAPSHOT_DEFAULT — indices, movers, sectors and sources each fall back to the seed with an lsShapeWarn recorded, and a missing asOf prints "an undated snapshot" rather than the word undefined. renderHealthMetrics guards the array, drops non-object rows, and on a wrong shape says so in the card instead of going blank. Executed after the fix: the garbage marketSnapshot renders "As of: an undated snapshot" with 2 shape warnings and 338 containers; a partly-wrong one records 3 warnings and still renders; healthMetrics as a string renders "The healthMetrics document is not a list, so this log cannot be drawn..."; a mixed-junk array renders the one valid row and drops the rest. No exceptions, no safeRun failures, 338 containers throughout.

area: Both artifacts — panels that render empty, checked against containersRendered's blind spot
finding: Swept every id'd element on both pages for a blank render and triaged the hits rather than trusting the count, because containersRendered only tracks innerHTML and misses anything built with textContent or appendChild. 25 elements on the portal and 162 on the deck render with no text; all of them turn out to be legitimate. Three classes account for them: rows built entirely from <input> elements, which have no textContent at all and so read as empty while rendering perfectly (assetItemRows was the clearest false positive — six real asset rows, zero characters); containers that fill only on an action (search results, council seat chips during a run, the hedge-fund run log, chat status notes); and cards whose explanation sits in a sibling note, which is the correct pattern — zhDealsStats renders nothing while zhDealsNote says "No zohoDeals document yet — the Deals module has never been read", and loftyStageStats renders nothing under an explaining loftySyncNote. The inverse blind spot also appeared: orNote is written with textContent, so it vanishes from containersRendered while rendering a full sentence — a container-count drop is not by itself evidence of a blank card, in either direction.
evidence: Scripted sweep over every id in both files under the runtime harness with each page's live store restored, reading textContent, 2026-09-23. Each candidate was then confirmed by reading its renderer and by --dump-text. Example: openrouterCredits injected as {a:1} drops one container (orNote) yet dump-text shows orNote = "Last refresh did not return a balance. Run the CLI by hand to see the raw error." and orBadge = "Sync failed". The genuine blank-with-no-reason cases found in this sweep are filed as F-Q3-03 and F-Q3-09 and are fixed.
fix: No change needed for the false positives. Recorded here so the next pass does not re-open them, and so the two-way blind spot in containersRendered is written down: a text-only card reads as unrendered, and an input-only card reads as empty.

area: command-deck.html — safeRun() and the render-failure surface, checked against the brief's silent-catch concern
finding: Checked whether the deck's safeRun swallows failures the way the brief warns, and it does not — verified rather than assumed. Its catch pushes {name, error} onto RENDER_FAILURES, and renderFailureAlerts() turns that into a critical notification carrying the renderer's name and the exact error message. The two pages surface it differently and both are defensible: the portal writes a banner into the panel region (isaRenderErrors), the deck routes it to the notification list. The deck's is weaker in one respect worth recording — the alert lives behind the bell icon rather than on the panel, so a failed card is blank in place with its explanation one click away — but it is surfaced, not swallowed, and the notification names both the renderer and the cause.
evidence: Injected reClients as a string before fixing F-Q3-03 and searched the rendered notifList: "1 panel failed to render — renderReClients (rows.forEach is not a function) — usually a document written in an unexpected shape. The rest of the page is unaffected." Badge showed 9+. One harness note for the next pass: the portal's RENDER_FAILURES holds label strings while the deck's holds {name, error} objects, so the harness reports the portal's safeRun failures as "undefined: undefined" — the page itself names them correctly, it is only the harness's report that is degraded.
fix: No change made to either mechanism. Recorded so the difference is a known, deliberate one rather than a finding the next pass re-raises.
